outcome.answer: Yes. The papers describe machine-learning approaches that detect early Alzheimer’s disease or mild cognitive impairment using clinical and cognitive measures, brain imaging, speech, and other behavioral signals [1, 2, 3, 6, 8]. One study reports that multimodal video, audio, and text models distinguish mild cognitive impairment from healthy aging [2], while another reports detection of mild cognitive impairment from changes across repeated behavioral sessions [3]. These are screening and classification results; the abstracts do not establish that the methods are ready to diagnose dementia in routine clinical use [1, 2, 3, 6, 8].
